Specimen & spectrum input JSON / schema 1

Edit the preloaded spectrum or choose a local JSON file. Loading a new input replaces the spectrum, not the cable positions. Invalid input leaves the last valid experiment intact. This fixture accepts 2 to 4,096 strictly increasing wavelengths (350–1,100 nm), corresponding nonnegative densities (up to 10 mW/nm), and authored-synthetic provenance only.

What is being simulated? Method & limits

Path, not drive electronics

The driver's electrical connection and both ends of the optical patch cable are independent prerequisites. A missing connection means no reading, not 0 mW. A fully connected receiver at 0% transmission can legitimately return 0 mW. Changes invalidate the previous result.

The input is a fictional piecewise-linear spectrum. The source integral is the sum of each wavelength interval times its average endpoint density. The ideal receiver multiplies every density by the same factor τ. No interpolation outside the input band and no estimate of real emitted power, fiber attenuation or biological response is made.

Independent area check: a triangle 20 nm wide and 0.1 mW/nm high has area 1.000 mW. At 40% transmission the receiver should report 0.400 mW. At 100% the spectra coincide. Receipts preserve the source identity, revision, units and synthetic provenance.

This study is not an operating manual or a calibrated device twin. It does not energize hardware, reproduce the driver electronics or model the OEM controls. The receiver, connector standoff and seating motion are authored teaching geometry. As a plug moves, its slack loop bends to maintain a fixed virtual centerline length (394 mm electrical; 170 mm fiber). Neither length is an OEM cable specification.

Handbooks and source photographs

  • Thorlabs · MxxxF1 family photograph · MxxxF1 Operation Manual, v1.3, 22 May 2012, cover. The finned black head has a captive dark electrical lead on one side and a separate SMA fiber patch cable on the other. This is a family photograph, not a serial-numbered M470F1.
  • Thorlabs · three-view outline drawing · MxxxF1 v1.3, §4.3, printed p. 22 (viewer p. 24). Orthographic top, front and side views distinguish the slotted flange, forward SMA bulkhead and back cable entry. Nominal dimensions are source drawings, not measurements of a physical sample.
  • Thorlabs · F1 connector / driver compatibility · MxxxF1 v1.3, §2, printed p. 4 (viewer p. 6). The male M8×1 electrical connector is on the end of the head cable. The manufacturer lists LEDD1B as a compatible driver. The SMA interface is optical, not another electrical connector.
  • Thorlabs · rear connector photograph · LEDD1B Operation Manual, 11 Jul 2018, M0009-510-515, §2.2, printed p. 7 (viewer p. 9). Facing the rear, the DC inlet is at left, metal BNC in the middle, and the smaller four-contact LED socket at right. The latter mates with the captive head lead.
  • Thorlabs · control panel photograph · LEDD1B, 2018, §3.1, printed p. 9 (viewer p. 11). The mode slider sits above a large rotary knob. CW, TRIG and MOD are physical landmarks; active driver electronics and settings are not simulated here.
  • Thorlabs · case and mounted envelope · LEDD1B, 2018, §5.1, printed p. 15 (viewer p. 17). The manual gives one set of dimensions without controls, and a larger assembly with controls and baseplate. This scene uses the bare case plus visible interface features, not the mounted assembly.
  • Thorlabs · archived M470F1 product record · M470F1 archive notice, 22 Mar 2016; product table and driver options. Identifies the 470 nm legacy head, family SMA fiber interface and the driver’s lack of EEPROM readout. The archive URL may open Thorlabs’ modern landing page; the linked family handbook supplies the geometry and compatibility independently.
  • M470F1 model index · link to Thorlabs handbook · Model index → Thorlabs MxxxF1 Operation Manual, 28 viewer pages. The item-specific manual index points to the legacy series handbook, not the newer M470F3.

What remains unverified

  • No measured device, physical calibration, material transfer or physical headset validation.
  • The 2012 handbook drawing is a shared F1-family outline applicable via the M470F1 manual index; not OEM device-specific CAD, detailed internal design, or a statement of tolerances.
  • Neither an exact serial-numbered M470F1 all-angles photographic set nor an independent comparison with bench measurements is available.
  • Detents, pose travel, cable routing, connector meshing and receiver placement are illustrative; no claim of specified torque, loss, connector tolerances or pin-level electrical simulation.
  • No OEM spectral output or calibrated optical measurements: the input spectrum and neutral transfer coefficient are explicitly synthetic.
